MAST30027: Simulation and Rejection Sampling

Week 9 - Solutions

Objectives of the Tutorial/Lab By the end of this tutorial, you should be able to:

  • Simulate marginal distributions under a Bayesian framework.
  • Simulate random variables using rejection sampling algorithm.
  • Verify that the simulated samples are consistent with the theoretical distribution.

Question 1

Suppose that X∼Bin(n,θ)X \sim \text{Bin}(n, \theta) and θ∼Beta(a,b)\theta \sim \text{Beta}(a,b). That is, X|θX|\theta has the pmf

pX|θ(x)=(nx)θx(1−θ)n−x p_{X|\theta}(x) = {n \choose x} \theta^x (1-\theta)^{n-x}

and θ\theta has pdf

fθ(x)=β(a,b)−1xa−1(1−x)b−1. f_\theta(x) = \beta(a,b)^{-1} x^{a-1}(1-x)^{b-1}.

The marginal distribution of XX is given by

pX(x)=∫01pX|θ(x)fθ(θ)dθ. p_X(x) = \int_0^1 p_{X|\theta}(x) f_\theta(\theta) d\theta.

XX is said to have a beta-binomial distribution. It is possible, but not easy, to work out pXp_X for a beta-binomial. However, it is easy to estimate it using simulation.

Generate a sample of size 1000,000 from a beta-binomial with n=10n = 10, a=2a = 2 and b=3b = 3. Use it to estimate the pmf of XX.

💡 Solution 
set.seed(300279)
N <- 1e6
tha <- rbeta(N, 2, 3)
X <- rbinom(N, 10, tha)
(p_X <- table(X)/N)
X
       0        1        2        3        4        5        6        7 
0.066230 0.109620 0.135315 0.144036 0.139627 0.125845 0.104476 0.079741 
       8        9       10 
0.054031 0.029951 0.011128 
plot(sort(unique(X)), p_X, type='h',xlab="X",
 ylab="probability", lwd=2,main="simulated pmf of X")

📈 Plotting it using ggplot2 
library(ggplot2)
pmf_df <- data.frame(X=as.numeric(names(p_X)), probability=as.numeric(p_X))
ggplot(pmf_df, aes(X, probability)) +
  geom_segment(aes(xend=X, y=0, yend=probability), linewidth=1) +
  labs(title="simulated pmf of X") + 
  theme_minimal()

Question 2

Suppose that Z follows a truncated exponential distribution, which has the pdf p(z)=e−z1−e−1p(z)=\frac{e^{-z}}{1-e^{-1}}, 0<z<10<z<1. Its theoretical mean and variance are known to be E(Z)=0.418E(Z) = 0.418 and Var(Z)=0.079\text{Var}(Z) = 0.079.

Construct an rejection sampling algorithm to generate a sample of observations from the truncated exponential distribution.

💡 Solution

When 0<z<10<z<1, p(z)<(1−e−1)−1<∞p(z)<(1-e^{-1})^{-1} < \infty, so we can use a rectangular envelope to contain the density. We get the following rejection algorithm:

  1. Generate X∼(0,1)X \sim (0,1).
  2. Generate Y∼(0,1/(1−e−1))Y \sim (0,1/(1-e^{-1})) independently.
  3. If Y≤p(X)Y \leq p(X) return XX; otherwise go to Step 11.

Write an R program to implement the algorithm in (a) and use it to generate a sample of 1000010000 observations. Plot a histogram of the sample. Calculate the sample mean and variance, and compare them with the theoretical mean and variance.

💡 Solution

We implement the algorithm in (a) and generate a sample of 10000 observations. We compute the sample mean and variance and compare them to the theoretical values. We also plot a histogram of the sample.

trunc_exp <- function(){
  # generate a truncated exponetial random variable using the rejection algorithm
  x <- runif(1)
  y <- runif(1, 0, 1/(1 - exp(-1)))
  while (y > exp(-x)/(1 - exp(-1))){
    x <- runif(1)
    y <- runif(1, 0, 1/(1 - exp(-1)))
  }
  return(x)
}

# generate a sample of size n
set.seed(30027)
n <- 10000
z <- rep(0, n)
for (i in 1:n) z[i] <- trunc_exp()
# sample mean and variance
mean(z)
[1] 0.4159879
var(z)
[1] 0.07836399
# histogram with density on top
hist(z, freq=FALSE, ylim=c(0,1.8))
curve(exp(-x)/(1 - exp(-1)), 0, 1, add=TRUE, col="red")

📈 Plotting it using ggplot2 
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(data.frame(z=z), aes(z)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y=after_stat(density)), breaks = seq(0, 1, length.out=20), colour="white") +
  stat_function(fun=function(x) exp(-x)/(1-exp(-1)), xlim=c(0,1), colour="red") +
  coord_cartesian(ylim=c(0,1.8)) + labs(x="z", y="Density") + 
  theme_minimal()

We can see that the sample mean and variance are similar to the theoretical values.
